items_missed: No real agenda statement with a time estimate ('takes about 10-15 minutes, sound good?') - only 'is it a convenient time to talk?'
Never asked whether the customer needs packing services, and never quoted packing pricing
Never asked about storage stops or additional stops
Never asked about moving stressors ('anything you're particularly worried about?')
No walk-distance discussion as a time variable, and no size equivalents (school bus reference) to make the 26-foot truck concrete

Save Your Ass was only half delivered - 'put the small items into your boxes yourself' with no consolidation examples (kids' toys, garden tools, loose drawer items, photos off walls) and no 'take a carload' tip
Weak booking ask - 'feel free to let us know' rather than an actual attempt to lock the date; the customer had to drive the booking himself
Never mentioned the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email or 'reply with any corrections'
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?'; gave contact methods but no business hours
Used the customer's name only twice ('Ryan')
No 60 cents/lb baseline alongside the No Worries coverage

Quote accuracy is questionable - she quoted 4 movers / 2 trucks / 9-10 hours / $5,010 off square footage alone after the customer said it's only two people with under 75 boxes and a sectional they may sell; she also described the drive as 'two hours away' (Riverview to St. Cloud is roughly an hour)
top_strength: The pricing and clock block was complete and confident - hourly rate, everything included, trip fee, No Worries $2,000, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, no-hidden-fees, clock start, 2.5 hour minimum and 15-minute increments all landed in one pass. She also handled the shop-around objection well by naming the specific hidden fees competitors use.
coaching_note: The quote was built off square footage instead of the items the customer actually described - he told her it's two people, under 75 boxes, possibly no sectional, and she still sent 4 movers and 2 trucks for $5,010 and then spent two minutes explaining why it might be wrong. Adjust the estimate live once the customer gives you the real inventory, or hold the number until the walkthrough - don't quote high and then walk it back.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and steady with regular 'no problem' / 'no worries' affirmations, but the pricing pitch was one long scripted block with no pauses or acknowledgment of the customer, and there were no rapport or humor moments.
audio_review_reason: Transcript is heavily garbled through the rep's scripted pricing and estimate blocks ('R weight', 'sterle fees', 'bunds', 'his first long as you need us'), which makes clarity and pace impossible to judge from text - worth a listen to confirm whether she is rushing the script.
